title: Plasmon Collapse in a Directional Strange Metal
authors: Jiade Li, Peiyi He, Deng Hu, Jiakai Wang, Jifeng Shao, Wan-Shun Du, Xuetao Zhu, Jiandong Guo, Zhiwei Wang, Peng Gao
abstract: Strange metals are widespread in strongly correlated quantum matter and closely intertwined with high-temperature superconductivity and quantum criticality, yet their microscopic charge dynamics remain fundamentally unresolved. Whether well-defined collective modes survive in an incoherent electronic fluid or dissolve into overdamped continua remains intensely debated. Here, employing high-momentum-resolution inelastic electron scattering complemented by direction-resolved transport, we show that the van der Waals compound $\mathrm{MoOCl}_2$, a "bad" metal known to host unusually "good" plasmons, exhibits a striking dichotomy in electronic coherence and charge dynamics. Transport reveals coherent Fermi liquid behavior along one in-plane crystallographic axis and an incoherent strange metal response along the orthogonal axis. This dichotomy extends directly to the charge response. The Fermi liquid direction supports a well-defined, long-lived plasmon, whereas the strange metal direction exhibits an overdamped excitation that progressively loses its collective character with increasing momentum. Beyond a critical momentum ($q_c$ $\approx$ 0.008 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-1}$), the mode undergoes a reversal into negative dispersion and ultimately collapses into a broad, nearly featureless continuum with a robust high-energy boundary ($E_c$ $\approx$ 1.75 eV). Remarkably, thickness-dependent measurements show that both $q_c$ and $E_c$ remain nearly unchanged despite substantial modifications of Coulomb screening, revealing them as intrinsic scales of incoherent charge density fluctuations. These results establish a unique single-material platform in which coherent and incoherent electronic states are partitioned into in-plane orthogonal channels, and demonstrate that incoherent electronic fluids retain intrinsically structured charge dynamics beyond the quasiparticle paradigm.
summary: This paper investigates charge dynamics in the strange metal $	ext{MoOCl}_2$ by comparing two orthogonal in-plane directions. It reveals that while one direction supports a well-defined plasmon, the other shows the plasmon collapsing into a featureless continuum. This establishes intrinsic energy and momentum scales that govern the incoherent electronic fluid, providing a unique test case for theories beyond the quasiparticle paradigm.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental unresolved question of charge dynamics in strange metals: whether well-defined collective modes survive in an incoherent electronic fluid or dissolve into overdamped continua.
main_result: The study demonstrates a striking dichotomy in $	ext{MoOCl}_2$, where one crystallographic direction supports a coherent plasmon (Fermi liquid behavior), while the orthogonal direction shows the plasmon collapsing into a featureless continuum bounded by an intrinsic energy scale ($E_c$).
method: The research combines high-momentum-resolution inelastic electron scattering (STEM-EELS) with direction-resolved transport measurements on $	ext{MoOCl}_2$ thin flakes.
model_or_system: The physical system is the van der Waals compound $	ext{MoOCl}_2$, which acts as a platform exhibiting coexisting, orthogonal electronic states—one behaving as a Fermi liquid and the other as a strange metal.
key_observables: Plasmon dispersion, resistivity ($ho$) vs. Temperature ($T$), critical momentum ($q_c$), and high-energy cutoff ($E_c$).
important_parameters: The intrinsic scales $q_c \approx 0.008 \mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-1}$ and $E_c \approx 1.75 	ext{ eV}$ are shown to be robust against changes in Coulomb screening (thickness).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to separate and compare charge dynamics along two orthogonal in-plane crystallographic axes, allowing for a direct comparison beyond the standard quasiparticle picture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the orthogonal electronic dichotomy via resistivity measurements and map the directional evolution of plasmon polaritons using STEM-EELS, showing clear propagation along one axis and collapse along the other.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the strange metal debate, presents the experimental setup using $	ext{MoOCl}_2$, details the orthogonal dichotomy observed in both transport and charge response, and concludes by identifying the intrinsic, robust scales governing the incoherent continuum.
why_interesting: The work provides a direct experimental platform to distinguish between coherent (quasiparticle-like) and incoherent charge dynamics in a strongly correlated material, offering insights into how collective excitations behave when the system deviates significantly from simple Fermi liquid theory.
